identityAssessment.finding: The imported 800 to 1000 record covers Ifriqiya approximately from 0.46 to 19.32 degrees east and 28.42 to 37.28 degrees north. It is the North African emirate, not a map of every raid or maritime connection. Its coverage extends beyond the verified 909 dynastic ending.

scopeNotes: The Fatimid destination is indexed from 1000 and has no 909 geometry; no successor navigation link is manufactured.

The pottery catalogue reverses terminus ante quem and post quem in its discussion of 876 and 909. The card uses the cautious stylistic attribution and explicit absence of excavation records, not the erroneous technical labels.
The minbar’s Indian wood, possible Baghdad associations and actual carving workshop are separate questions.
The mosque’s eleventh-century maqsura and other later features are not assigned to Aghlabid patrons.
Inconsistent reservoir dimensions in public descriptions are not repeated.
The coin transcription does not visibly give a prince’s name despite the catalogue’s general statement; only its explicitly transcribed date and emblem are claimed.
No post-Aghlabid Geniza evidence or disputed Blue Qur’an origin is projected into the ninth century.
